 Learn more "The 8:30" hosts Julie Hyman, Pras Subramanian, and Jake Conley discuss mounting challenges for Nvidia ( NVDA ) as the AI chip giant reportedly faces a California subpoena related to its chip sales in China. The panel examines the potential regulatory fallout, questions surrounding investor disclosures, and what increased scrutiny could mean for Nvidia's business.

Uh, Alibaba, for example, getting 75,000 chips, um, from the US, 10 cent getting 150,000. And some of these companies have been briefly put on a designation by the Pentagon that would connect them to the Chinese military. 10 cent, uh, was on a list, is still is on a list connecting it to the Chinese military. And the questions that have been opened up is, not only was Nvidia selling chips to Megaspeed who was then maybe moving them on to China around export controls, but was that getting as far as the Chinese military, which then opens up a huge ream of national security questions. All this is going to be in focus when Jensen Huang, when Under Secretary for Commerce Jeff Kessler, when Howard Lutnick, the Department of Commerce secretary, start testifying in a couple of weeks. These are going to be some hard questions and now they've got subpoenas from California to answer.
